changes.classification: no effect on the enforced no-discussion handoff slice
changes.reason: Imports canRetireDiscussionWork and narrows the ended-task skip in TeamEngine.recover only when an intent is safely retirable obsolete discussion work. The slice explicitly excludes every discussionId, so the predicate is false and ordinary ended tasks keep the original skip behavior. No send/flush transaction is split or merged.

harnessChanges: compare.mjs observe now explicitly rejects any intent carrying discussionId. This makes the guard input added by the product fix visible at every replay observation, rather than relying only on the existing absence of current discussion/decomposition/local-operation state.
correspondence: submit -> claim A -> HELP -> claim B -> RECORD_RESULT creates one ordinary assistance without discussionId. Handoff graph actions only flush/direct/retry/duplicate/stop/continue/change-goal/crash/rollback/reopen; none creates discussion-tagged work. Thus canRetireDiscussionWork is false in the complete enforced slice, while all existing non-discussion RECOVER branches, result markers, unique owner creation, stop cancellation and transaction boundaries are preserved.
candidateProcedure: After reading every changed covered file and preserving the original blocked evidence, only candidate file hashes are refreshed while syncCommit remains at the prior verified commit. Run the complete finite model, both-store graph replays, all reachability witnesses and all four real-code behavioral negative controls; promote syncCommit only after verified plus independent evidence readback.
limits: The handoff finite graph does not prove discussion/MapReduce cancellation recovery, participant occupancy, LOCAL_RESULT/LOCAL_RECONCILE retirement or physical-effect safety. The coordination maintenance and BT_Q19-Q23 provide separate bounded evidence. No theorem about the Cartesian product of those protocols is added. The ended-task selection branch in TeamEngine.recover is statically reviewed here but not dynamically traversed by the handoff graph; separate public-recovery coordination instances cover that behavior.
